page.layout: One page of verse, single column; running head at top; page number top left; a large initial L and N in the text; a marginal note column on the right edge of the text containing a few marks (no printed words in the margins beyond the Greek-style marks and a stray "Nec" at the foot which is part of the verse).

p.l: L Ena parens Leonora tibi est, & filia lena est,
Lena est, quae faciem viscida creta tegit,
Et quot habet vetulas vicinia sunt tibi lenae,
Et lena est toto fisci na nota foro,
Quàm bene vix tandem tot possunt vendere lenae,
Haud equidem mercem suspicor esse bonam.
S Ors tibi nominibus nocuit male grata duobus
Quod dederit sophiae, stultitiaque parum.
Si tibi stultitia plus esset, stultus haberi.
Posses, si sophia plus foret, esse sophos.
At tu μωρόσοφος sapiens es morio, stultus
Es sapiens, & nec morio, nec sapiens.
Nunc tamen ut Curius praesentia facula damnas,
Nunc stolida fingis garrulitate iocos:
At sophiam simulans per longas proderis aures:
Dissimulans sophiam, dissimulare nequis.
Unde igitur vives nulla Mida praeditus arte,
Si tibi nec stulto, nec licet esse sopho.
N Æuole dum clamas, ut stentora vincere possis,
Omnis homo est animal nocte diéque boans,
Iam tibi dilapsa est prope nonagesima messis,
Iam tremit invalido curva senecta gradu:
Vertice iam lavi vix tres hasere capilli,
Et cernus, quantum noctua mane videt.
Semper & e gelido distillat stirna naso,
Et fluit in madidos longa saliua sinus:
Nec tibi gingiua dens unus & alter inermi est:
Nec

page.notes: Marginal marks on the right edge are ornamental/show-through and not transcribed. The Greek word μωρόσοφος is copied as printed. The final "Nec" stands at the bottom right, probably a catchword. The initial letters L and N are large woodcut-style initials joined to their words. Some words in the verse are uncertain and not marked, e.g. "stirna" and "Cernus".
